task.name: cut-rc.sh requires the operator to know and pass the next RC number by hand
task.story_text:
## What happened

`scripts/cut-rc.sh` takes `RC_NUM` as an optional positional argument that defaults to `0` — it does not look at what RC tags already exist. Once a release line has more than one RC, invoking the script with just `VERSION` always tries to cut `rc0` again, fails on the existing-tag check, and tells the operator to bump `RC_NUM` by hand:

```
Error: tag v0.13.0rc2 already exists on origin. Bump RC_NUM.
```

The operator has to separately query which RC tags exist (`git tag --list`, or trial-and-error against the script's own refusal) before every cut past the first.

## Expected

Invoking the script with only `VERSION` cuts the next RC number after the highest `v<VERSION>rcN` tag that exists on origin, so a repeat cut on an active release line needs no operator lookup. An explicit `RC_NUM` argument continues to work as an override, and the existing collision guards (tag already exists locally / on origin) stay in place as a backstop in case the computed number is wrong for any reason.

## Example

Before, on a line with `rc0`/`rc1`/`rc2` already tagged:

```
$ scripts/cut-rc.sh 0.13.0
Error: tag v0.13.0rc0 already exists on origin. Bump RC_NUM.
```

requiring the operator to know `rc3` is next and pass it explicitly:

```
$ scripts/cut-rc.sh 0.13.0 3
```

After, the first invocation alone cuts `rc3`:

```
$ scripts/cut-rc.sh 0.13.0
Cutting RC      : 0.13.0rc3
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/cut-rc.sh VERSION` with no `RC_NUM` reports and cuts the RC number one past the highest existing `v<VERSION>rcN` tag on origin, rather than always attempting `rc0`.
- [ ] `scripts/cut-rc.sh VERSION` on a release line with no existing RC tags still cuts `rc0`, unchanged from today.
- [ ] Passing an explicit `RC_NUM` continues to override the computed number.
- [ ] The existing tag-already-exists checks (local and origin) still run as a guard, in case the computed or overridden number collides.
- [ ] `--resume` is unaffected: it continues to resume the same `VERSION`/`RC_NUM` the original (possibly auto-computed) invocation targeted, not a freshly recomputed number.

handoff.summary: Replaced cut-rc.sh's unconditional `RC_NUM="${RC_NUM:-0}"` default with resolution from origin. A new highest_origin_rc() helper queries `git ls-remote --tags origin refs/tags/v<VERSION>rc*`, extracts numeric suffixes and takes the numeric max; the script then cuts highest+1, or rc0 when the release line has no RC tags. An explicit RC_NUM argument short-circuits the computation. Under --resume with no RC_NUM the script resolves to the highest existing tag (the RC the aborted cut targeted) rather than a fresh next number, and errors if no RC tag exists to resume. An unreachable origin fails loud instead of silently guessing rc0. The resolved number and its derivation are printed in the header block. Both tag-already-exists guards (local rev-parse, origin ls-remote) are unchanged and still run after resolution. Docs updated in RELEASING.md and docs/guides/controller-runbook.md (the runbook's `RC_NUM=n scripts/cut-rc.sh` env-var form was already wrong — the script zeroes RC_NUM before argv parsing — and is now the positional/auto form). 11 new subprocess tests drive the real script against a git shim whose ls-remote answers from a configurable tag list using real glob semantics.

acceptance_criteria.notes: Both guards are unmodified and still inside the RESUME==false branch after RC_NUM resolution. Covered by test_origin_tag_collision_guard_still_refuses_a_colliding_number and test_local_tag_collision_guard_still_runs.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: --resume is unaffected: it continues to resume the same VERSION/RC_NUM the original (possibly auto-computed) invocation targeted, not a freshly recomputed number.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Explicit RC_NUM under --resume is honoured verbatim (test_resume_with_explicit_rc_num_targets_that_rc). For --resume with no RC_NUM — previously a silent default to rc0 — the script now resolves to the highest existing origin tag, which by definition is what the aborted cut pushed (test_resume_without_rc_num_targets_highest_existing_tag asserts rc2, not rc3), and errors when no RC tag exists to resume (test_resume_without_rc_num_fails_when_no_rc_tags_exist). Flagged below as the one interpretive call.

story_deviations: The AC says --resume must be 'unaffected'. Read literally, --resume with no RC_NUM would keep defaulting to rc0 — which on any line past rc0 fails the resume-requires-tag-on-origin check. I read the AC's intent as 'must not resume a freshly computed NEXT number' and resolved it to the highest existing origin tag instead, which is provably the RC the aborted cut targeted (that cut pushed the tag before aborting). Explicit-RC_NUM resume behaviour is byte-identical to before.

Fixed an adjacent doc error found while updating: docs/guides/controller-runbook.md documented `RC_NUM=n scripts/cut-rc.sh X.Y.Z`, an env-var form the script never supported (it sets RC_NUM="" before parsing argv). Replaced with the positional/auto form.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
